concoctions.name: Fermented Plant Juice
concoctions.description: A natural fertilizer made from the fermented sap and chlorophyll of vigorous plants, capturing their enzymatic energy and nutrients.
concoctions.purpose: Provides a high concentration of Nitrogen (N) and natural growth hormones to the plants.
procedure: Collect young plant shoots or nitrogen-rich leaves (e.g., Kakawate) early in the morning.
Finely chop the materials to maximize nutrient extraction.
Mix the chopped materials with molasses at a 1:1 ratio by weight.
If the plant material is particularly dry, increase the amount of molasses to ensure proper fermentation.
Store in a container and ferment for 7 days.

application.stage: Use during the vegetative or growing stage.

concoctions.name: Fermented Fruit Juice
concoctions.description: A liquid fertilizer derived from sweet, potassium-rich fruits, often referred to as 'plant food' for the reproductive phase.
concoctions.purpose: Rich in Potassium (K); acts as a taste enhancer to improve the sweetness of the harvest.
procedure: Use sweet, ripe fruits such as bananas or papayas.
Chop the fruits into small pieces.
Mix thoroughly with molasses at a 1:1 ratio.
Place in a covered container and ferment for 7 days.

application.stage: Apply during the flowering and fruiting stages.

concoctions.name: Fish Amino Acid
concoctions.description: A nutrient-dense liquid produced from fermented fish waste, providing a diverse profile of nitrogen and minerals.
concoctions.purpose: A general-purpose fertilizer providing NPK, Calcium, and Magnesium.
procedure: Collect fish scraps, entrails, or chopped whole fish.
Mix the fish material with molasses at a 1:1 ratio.
Seal the container and allow it to ferment for 7 days.

concoctions.name: Indigenous Microorganisms
concoctions.description: A culture of beneficial local microbes harvested from the environment to restore soil biological health.
concoctions.purpose: Recharges the soil with beneficial bacteria and accelerates the decomposition of organic matter.
procedure: Place half-cooked rice into a bamboo container.
Cover with paper and plastic to protect from rain and leave for 3 to 5 days until white mold appears.
Harvest the molded rice and mix it with molasses at a 1:1 ratio.
Ferment the mixture for another 7 days (12 days total process).

application.frequency: Apply consistently during the 1-to-2-week land-resting period before planting.

concoctions.name: Lactic Acid Bacteria Serum
concoctions.description: A resilient probiotic serum containing lactic acid bacteria, which improves digestion in animals and nutrient uptake in plants.
concoctions.purpose: A probiotic serum used to improve soil health and livestock digestion.
procedure: Phase 1: Ferment rice wash (water from the first wash of rice) for 1 week.
Phase 2: Extract the liquid and add milk at a 1:9 ratio (1 part rice wash to 9 parts milk).
Ferment for 1 week.
Phase 3: Extract the middle 'yellow' liquid (the serum) and mix with molasses at a 1:1 ratio.
Ferment for a final 1 week.

application.stage: General use for soil or livestock.
application.dilution: 10mL/L for plants; up to 20mL/L for livestock drinking water.

concoctions.name: Calcium Phosphate
concoctions.description: A solution extracted from roasted organic calcium sources using vinegar to make the minerals water-soluble and plant-available.
concoctions.purpose: Prevents flower and fruit drop by strengthening the plant's reproductive structures.
procedure: Clean eggshells or bones and roast/pan-heat them until slightly browned to enrich the phosphorus.
Crush or chop the roasted materials into small pieces.
Submerge the pieces in natural vinegar (e.g., coconut or sugar palm vinegar) at a 1:9 ratio.
Allow the mixture to sit and ferment for 21 days.

application.stage: Apply during the flowering and fruiting stages.

concoctions.name: Oriental Herbal Nutrient
concoctions.description: A traditional herbal extract used as a natural prophylactic and pest deterrent, strengthening the plant from the inside out.
concoctions.purpose: Serves as a natural pest repellent and plant immune system booster.
procedure: Finely chop aromatic herbs (e.g., ginger, garlic, oregano, or citronella).
Phase 1: Mix herbs with molasses and ferment for 3 to 5 days.
Phase 2: Add natural vinegar to the mixture (approx. 700mL vinegar per 400mL molasses) and ferment for another 5 to 7 days.

general_maintenance_standards.storage_environment: Store all containers in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight.

shelf_life.duration: Concoctions are at peak quality for 6 months.
shelf_life.warning: Beyond this, the microbes may deplete the available food (molasses), reducing potency.

general_maintenance_standards.sanitation: Always clean materials before processing and ensure containers are sealed properly to avoid contamination from flies or pests.

quality_indicators.success: A successful batch should have a sweet-sour, fermented aroma.
quality_indicators.failure: A foul or putrid smell indicates contamination, and the batch should be discarded.
